evidence_quotes.quote: O presente artigo tem como objetivo apresentar um panorama da tarifa social no Brasil e verificar como as diferentes formas de prestação do serviço influenciam: (i) a incidência da tarifa social, em termos do número de municípios que apresentam o benefício; (ii) o alcance social da tarifação social, em termos do número de potenciais usuários de fato beneficiados; e (iii) o comprometimento da renda dos beneficiários.

evidence_quotes.page: Section 2.1. Construção do panorama da tarifação social no Brasil
evidence_quotes.quote: Um panorama da tarifa social no Brasil foi elaborado a partir do levantamento e sistematização de dados do Sistema Nacional de Informações sobre Saneamento (SNIS) e do sistema de Consulta, Seleção e Extração de Informações do CadÚnico, ambos referentes ao ano de 2021.

evidence_quotes.page: Section 4.3 Critérios de enquadramento na tarifa social
evidence_quotes.quote: A análise de correlação de Spearman mostrou que o número de critérios de enquadramento na tarifa social e o percentual de economias beneficiadas em relação aos cadastrados no CadÚnico apresentam relação estatisticamente significativa (p-valor = 0,018) e apresentam correlação negativa moderada (ρ = -0,521).

evidence_quotes.page: Section 4.2.1 Economias beneficiadas em relação ao total de economias
evidence_quotes.quote: Em relação ao total de economias, no país como um todo, os prestadores públicos beneficiam com tarifa social 5,3% das economias, enquanto os prestadores privados beneficiam 3,9%.

evidence_quotes.page: Section 4.4 Comprometimento da renda dos usuários na tarifa social
evidence_quotes.quote: Considerando uma família com renda de um salário mínimo, tem-se que os únicos cinco prestadores que apresentam tarifa social média que supera 3% do salário mínimo vigente na época são privados.

criterion_notes.c1: Examines economic access (affordability and social tariff access/exclusion) for household water supply and water-and-sewage sanitation services in Brazil.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type clarification: under the plain wording, it examines regulatory tariff policy, institutional service-delivery models, and eligibility governance; under the narrow rule-type reading, it directly analyzes tariff/cost-recovery subsidy rules (social tariffs), eligibility screening and documentation criteria (number and types of enrollment criteria), and utility ownership/corporate structure (public, private, closed-capital and open-capital mixed-economy corporations) governing household affordability and access to tariff benefits.
criterion_notes.c3: Quantitative cross-sectional empirical study analyzing 2021 administrative micro/provider-level and state-level data from SNIS and CadÚnico using descriptive statistics, GIS mapping, and Spearman rank correlation.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports municipality-level availability of social tariffs, household/account social tariff coverage (% of total economias and % of water-connected CadÚnico low-income families receiving the social tariff, capturing administrative exclusion), and affordability (mean social tariff prices and % of 1-minimum-wage household income committed vs. the 3% UN benchmark).
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies the study design (cross-sectional observational study of 2021 SNIS and CadÚnico administrative records), units of analysis and population (Brazilian water and water-and-sewage utilities, municipalities, states/UFs, and CadÚnico-registered low-income families with water network access), exposures (utility ownership/scope model and number/type of social tariff eligibility criteria), and access/affordability outcomes.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Portuguese (with English and Portuguese abstracts), which is directly eligible without translation under Criterion 9.

study_design: Cross-sectional quantitative observational study of administrative data (SNIS and CadÚnico, 2021) using descriptive comparative analysis, GIS mapping, and Spearman rank correlation.
population_and_sample: Brazilian water supply and water-and-sewage service providers reporting to SNIS in 2021 (excluding sewage-only and direct municipal administration providers without tariff data), analyzed across Brazilian municipalities, all 27 federative units (UFs), and low-income families registered in CadÚnico with piped water network access.
exposure: Water and sanitation utility ownership and service-delivery model (local/microregional public vs. private; regional public/autarky, private, closed-capital mixed-economy corporation, and open-capital mixed-economy corporation) and social tariff eligibility screening rules (number and type of enrollment criteria).
outcome: Social tariff availability across municipalities, social tariff reach/coverage (% of total water/sanitation economias and % of piped-water-connected CadÚnico low-income families receiving the social tariff), and water/sanitation affordability (mean social tariff level and % of a 1-minimum-wage family income committed).
rationale: This Portuguese-language empirical study meets all inclusion criteria (c1–c6). Using 2021 national administrative data from SNIS and CadÚnico, it empirically evaluates rule-type legal, regulatory, and institutional mechanisms directly governing economic access to household water and sanitation services in Brazil—specifically utility ownership/corporate governance models, tariff subsidy rules, and social tariff eligibility screening criteria—and reports clear outcomes on social tariff availability, beneficiary coverage/exclusion among low-income households, and tariff affordability relative to minimum-wage income.
